A1.justification: Both PDFs are complete, readable 38-page versions of the same BlackSwanSuite paper. Text, tables, figures, algorithms, and screenshot appendices can be matched despite reflow and appendix renumbering.

before.justification: v1 reports original VLM and human evaluations, dataset-quality measurements, and perception, chain-of-thought, and hard-subset experiments, including appendix results.

after.justification: v2 retains those original empirical results and adds validation/test-specific benchmark scores in Appendix G.

M1.justification: The video-splitting algorithm, annotation and question-construction procedures, task inputs, and inference prompts are retained. The new reasoning taxonomy explains existing tasks without changing their procedures.

E1.justification: Both evaluate the same 1,655 Oops! videos and seven Forecaster, Detective, and Reporter task variants. The new validation/test partitions divide existing coverage rather than introduce new datasets or task requirements.

E2.justification: The six principal VLMs, human comparisons, and additional LLaVA-Video-72B comparisons are retained. The new leaderboard tables reuse existing VLM comparators without changing membership in the corresponding original experiments.

E3.justification: New Appendix G introduces a leaderboard partition: 827 validation videos with accessible labels and 828 test videos with hidden labels, containing 95 and 224 hard-subset videos respectively. This adds an evaluation arrangement within the retained benchmark; the original experiments and metrics remain.

E4.justification: The displayed perception/comprehension controls, chain-of-thought experiments, hard-subset analysis, and qualitative cases are unchanged. v2 adds pointers to examples.mp4, but the supplied PDFs contain no additional inspectable analysis from that external video.

E5.justification: Point-estimate reporting and human-rater aggregation remain unchanged. No repeated-run counts, seeds, confidence intervals, or statistical significance procedures are introduced by the additional result tables.

E6.justification: Tables 13–16 add validation/test scores for the existing models. For example, GPT-4o Detective MCQ accuracy is reported as 67.2% on validation and 63.2% on test, alongside the retained full-dataset 65.1%. These are additional partition-specific results, not same-setting gains. Earlier main and appendix results are retained.

T1.justification: The abductive and defeasible reasoning definitions and Algorithm 1's mathematical splitting rules are unchanged. Appendix A's reasoning classification is conceptual explanation, without new formal assumptions, derivations, or proofs.

C1.justification: The central contribution remains a benchmark for reasoning about unexpected events, with 15,469 questions and substantial human–VLM gaps. Naming evaluated models in the revised abstract and rewording the conclusion do not change these claims.

C2.justification: v2 makes the generative-metric caveats more task-specific and explicitly maps task variants to reasoning types. Appendix G newly characterizes the test partition as harder because it contains more hard-subset videos. Existing limitations are consolidated into Appendix I rather than newly introduced.

D1.justification: v2 adds explicit leaderboard and label-access information, plus directions to a supplementary examples.mp4 file. Existing model identifiers, frame counts, prompts, annotation requirements, and evaluation templates remain unchanged; the external video's contents cannot be verified from the PDFs.

R1.justification: The same 46 cited works and positioning against prior abductive, defeasible, and video-reasoning benchmarks are retained. The added statement that this is the first such task restates v1's existing claim that prior work had not addressed this setting.

P1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and results receive wording and paragraph edits; headings and task terminology are refined. New appendix sections organize reasoning types and leaderboard results, while existing limitations are merged into one section. The overall narrative structure remains recognizable.

P2.justification: v2 adds the reasoning-classification table and four leaderboard tables, relocates several existing figures and tables, and adjusts captions. The figure content and screenshot appendices are retained. Table 2 newly mislabels its tasks as Forecaster and Detective despite retaining Detective and Reporter column headings.

improvement.justification: The reasoning summary and documented validation/test access policy improve clarity and usability. However, new split results are not reconciled with retained scores: VideoChat2 Detective Y/N accuracy is 63.0% in Table 2 but 63.9% and 63.8% in Tables 13–14, with no explained protocol difference. The new Table 2 caption error also reduces clarity. These unresolved reporting issues prevent a reliable judgment of net quality improvement.
